subject.title: fix(cron): detect ===DONE_ERR=== sentinel in agent final text as failure signal

question: Should a final assistant reply beginning with `===DONE_ERR===` become a supported cron failure protocol, or should cron continue to require typed `failureSignal`/runtime errors?
rationale: Current code and the unattended-cron prompt establish structured failure ownership but no reserved text sentinel, so accepting this classifier changes the public behavior and false-positive boundary rather than repairing an established contract.

options.title: Keep structured failure ownership
options.body: Remove the text classifier and route any agent failure through the existing typed `failureSignal` or run-level outcome path.

options.title: Adopt a supported sentinel protocol
options.body: Define the exact producing runtime, grammar, false-positive policy, documentation, and end-to-end cron alert proof before accepting text as a fatal signal.

recommendation.title: Keep structured failure ownership
recommendation.body: Remove the text classifier and route any agent failure through the existing typed `failureSignal` or run-level outcome path.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main owner trail could not be safely established without git history; a cron/runtime owner should decide the terminal-state contract.
